summary: Ephemeral runner keystore permission churn causing intermittent auth failures during Vault path rename
description:
Issue summary: During an automated Vault path rename performed as part of a tenant split, a subset of ephemeral CI runners started failing job authentication with errors indicating keystore access denied. Failures are intermittent and correlate with the time window when the vault-mount-controller re-writes secret paths and the secret-sync agent reconciles nodes.

Impact: Multiple ephemeral runners in prod/us-east failed to fetch deploy keys or sign payloads for ~8 minutes, causing ~5% of nightly release and PR pipelines to error out. No customer-facing API impact; CI pipelines for internal releases were delayed.

Observed behavior: Runners report failing to read /var/lib/runner/keystore/private.pem with permission denied. On restart some runners recover, others require manual chown/chmod. The pattern suggests ownership/perm churn rather than persistent corruption.

Expected behavior: Vault path rename should be applied without leaving transient permission mismatches on runner keystore files. Secret-sync should maintain atomic handover semantics so runner processes don’t observe permission oscillation.

Frequency: Occurred during this Vault maintenance window (March 12) and reproduced reliably when the vault-mount-controller performs a rename operation under high concurrency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In prod us-east, create a test secret path mounts/runner-keys-v1 and populate keystore files via secret-sync.
2) Simulate concurrent rename: issue Vault API call to rename mounts/runner-keys-v1 -> mounts/runner-keys-v2 while scaling secret-sync replicas to 3.
3) Run a batch of ephemeral jobs that attempt to read /var/lib/runner/keystore/private.pem during the rename window.
4) Observe intermittent permission denied errors in runner logs; some runners briefly report file owner as uid 0 then uid 1001 in <10s windows.
5) Restarting the runner process recovers it in ~60s for some instances; others require manual chown to recover.
logs: 2026-03-12T02:14:22Z secret-sync-0 secret-sync[47]: INFO writing to /var/lib/runner/keystore/private.pem (uid=1001 gid=1001 mode=0600)
2026-03-12T02:14:22Z secret-sync-1 secret-sync[49]: INFO removing old path mounts/runner-keys-v1 -> moved
2026-03-12T02:14:22Z runner-xyz987 /usr/local/bin/runner[3400]: WARN observed keystore owner changed from uid 0 to uid 1001 while open file descriptor active
2026-03-12T02:14:23Z kubelet node-12 kubelet[1223]: Event: FilePermsChanged /var/lib/runner/keystore/private.pem (uid:gid sequence mismatch)
investigation_notes: Initial triage by on-call SRE (Priya Desai): verified Vault rename operation and secret-sync logs; timestamps line up with runner errors.

Hypothesis: secret-sync instances are performing a write-then-delete handoff without acquiring a coordination lock, causing transient owner/permission flips that break open file descriptors in long-lived runner processes.

Observed that some runner instances keep an open FD to the file; when the backing file is atomically replaced, kernel shows new inode with different owner while FD still points to old inode; however permission checks on subsequent reads honor new inode attributes leading to EACCES.
kubectl exec into affected pod and ran: stat -c '%u:%g %a %i' /var/lib/runner/keystore/private.pem -> showed alternating inode numbers and owners between concurrent secret-sync writes.

Checked secret-sync code path: current implementation uses rename(2) to replace files but does not preserve ownership or coordinate with any pod-level lock. The runner process expects stable owner uid 1001.
Cross-reference: linked to prior issue INT-26411 (vault-rewrap-related injection failures) which surfaced secret-sync edge cases during bulk operations.
comments: Marisol Nguyen (reporter) - 2026-03-12: Noticed ~10% failure rate in internal CI during the maintenance window. Attached runner logs and sample pod names.
Priya Desai (SRE oncall) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed correlation with Vault rename. Recommending immediate mitigation: pause secret-sync rolling updates and drain new rename jobs.

Ethan Patel (assignee) - 2026-03-12: I will coordinate a staged restart of secret-sync replicas with a reconcile script to avoid concurrent writes. Planning follow-up fix in runner-operator to add file-level coordination.
Runner Team (infra) - 2026-03-13: Added a quick fix PR to runner-bootstrap to have the runner reopen FD on ENOENT/EACCES for keystore reads as a band-aid (see related PR).
Priya Desai - 2026-03-13: Ran remediation script on 4 affected nodes; jobs resumed. Keeping ticket open for long-term automation and root cause patch.
resolution:
Workaround applied: paused the Vault path rename rollout, drained secret-sync controllers, and applied a staged reconciliation script that re-applies correct uid:gid and atomically symlinks rather than replacing files in-place. Short-term runner code change added a retry path to reopen keystore FDs on EACCES with backoff (PR https://github.com/redwood/runner-bootstrap/pull/233).

Long-term fix: implement a coordination lock in secret-sync to make renames atomic from the consumer perspective (create new path, set ownership, then update a single symlink), and add an operator-level precondition to block concurrent rename operations. Proposed follow-up PR: https://github.com/redwood/runner-operator/pull/8912.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem with release engineering and secret-sync owners scheduled (Confluence page linked).
- Add automated test in CI that simulates concurrent renames and validates runner keystore stability.
next_steps: 1) Merge and roll out runner-bootstrap reopen-on-eacces patch to staging, validate with synthetic jobs.
2) Add coordination/lock to secret-sync and test in canary cluster before prod rollouts.
3) Update runbook to include 'pause secret-sync' step before vault path renames and add an automated gate check in release-orchestrator.
4) Complete postmortem and add monitoring alert for file owner churn on /var/lib/runner/keystore.
